assumptions: The evaluated wedge is limited to module linear-performance-warranty screening and evidence dossiers for commercial rooftop portfolios, not continuous monitoring, general O&M, legal representation, or broad claims administration.
O&M firms, lessors, or owners can lawfully provide customer-authorised contracts, serial records, site history, maintenance evidence, and exported telemetry needed for screening.
Revenue is evaluated on prepaid batch screening and fixed dossier fees; no monitoring revenue, recovery fee, claimed recovery rate, or claimed margin improvement is assumed.
Accredited testing, electrical work, legal interpretation, and insurance are separately scoped and priced rather than absorbed into the desk fee.
The stated 2,000-6,000 PLN dossier price and 55-70% desk gross-margin range are planning hypotheses whose feasibility remains unknown rather than established economics.
Any compounding outcome corpus can be retained only with appropriate permission and privacy controls; access to reusable outcome data is not assumed.
The cited research findings are accepted as the available evidence packet, and no additional market facts are inferred beyond it.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid batches from multiple unrelated O&M firms or lessors showing minimum efficient batch size, record-complete and contract-eligible rates, screen-to-test and test-to-manufacturer-acceptance rates, verified recovery or avoided-cost value, resolution time, fully loaded labor/legal/testing/insurance cost, contribution margin, partner CAC/payback, and repeat submissions after the first batch.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept identifies a credible gap between cheap monitoring and expensive field testing: fragmented small-asset service economics, manufacturer-specific proof burdens, and misleading underperformance signals make a document-first eligibility screen useful. Portfolio batching is a coherent response to the small-system economics documented in the packet. The insight is narrower and sharper than a generic monitoring service, although the frequency of economically recoverable cases remains unknown.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Avoiding unnecessary accredited tests and advancing a valid warranty claim can create meaningful value for a portfolio operator, while record reconstruction and procedural proof are real burdens. However, the packet contains no paid demand, partner commitment, recovery distribution, or evidence that buyers will prepay at the proposed price. Low-cost Polish service plans that include warranty handling also constrain willingness to pay unless this specialized screen demonstrably changes outcomes or avoids larger costs.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid batches, fixed dossier fees, hard go/no-go gates, and separately authorised testing improve cash conversion and cap downside compared with open-ended recovery work. The desk component could have attractive gross margin and automation leverage. Yet batch size, pass rate, case-handling time, testing and liability cost, repeat frequency, and realized customer benefit are unknown, so the proposed pricing and 55-70% margin cannot yet support a credible owner-earnings or 5 million PLN founder-net-worth path.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Independent Polish O&M firms and lessors with commercial rooftop portfolios form a specific, identifiable beachhead, and Poland's large PV base supplies a plausible asset pool. The evidence does not isolate the target segment or show how many sites simultaneously have material module underperformance, live warranty rights, complete records, and sufficient recovery value. The segment is narrow enough to serve, but its economically eligible case volume is not yet shown to be meaningful.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Specialising in one warranty archetype and sitting before costly testing creates a credible workflow position, especially as a neutral white-label desk. However, existing service providers already offer monitoring and warranty administration cheaply, and capable O&M firms or lessors may internalise a visible screening checklist. No exclusive access, manufacturer recognition, or contracted partner channel currently supports a dominant position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful module-warranty workflow could extend to more manufacturers, additional O&M and lessor portfolios, and adjacent evidence-heavy PV warranty protocols. Each expansion could reuse document extraction, telemetry normalisation, and partner relationships. Expansion is not frictionless, because contracts, failure modes, test standards, and manufacturer procedures vary and may require fresh specialist work rather than simple software replication.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A permissioned corpus connecting screening inputs, test decisions, manufacturer responses, and verified outcomes could gradually improve triage accuracy and switching costs. At inception the process is largely replicable, vendor and customer data rights are uncertain, and partners may withhold outcomes or copy the workflow. The proposed moat therefore depends on scale and permissions that have not been established.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer is meaningfully more focused than generic monitoring: it screens contract and record eligibility, excludes curtailment and ordinary causes, and prevents testing spend on clearly weak cases. That can improve speed, consistency, and risk control for partners lacking specialist capacity. The magnitude of avoided cost, acceptance uplift, turnaround improvement, and price advantage has not been measured, so behavior-changing superiority is plausible but unproven.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Poland's growing installed PV base and the accumulating age of assets create a plausible future flow of performance questions, while accessible irradiance data and AI-assisted document review lower desk-work cost. At the same time, curtailment and multiple ordinary degradation mechanisms increase false-positive risk, and the packet does not show a current wave of recoverable module-warranty cases. Timing is favorable but not uniquely urgent.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Selling white-label batches to a limited set of portfolio aggregators is more repeatable and founder-compatible than acquiring individual owners, and permissioned family-network records provide a low-cost learning route. No referral or purchasing commitment is assumed, however, and target partners may see the service as unnecessary, negotiate away margin, or submit only low-quality cases. Repeatable acquisition and partner CAC/payback remain unvalidated.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The narrow, batch-based desk fits the founder's analytical skills, renewable-energy access, available capital, and part-time constraint, while field, legal, and accredited-test work can be delegated. Execution still requires reliable multi-source records, protocol expertise, quality control, professional-liability boundaries, and dependable specialist partners. Manufacturer variation and ambiguous causation can make apparently standardized cases bespoke, but the gated scope makes these risks manageable enough to test.

highest_value_structural_change: Turn ad hoc batch sales into a minimum-volume annual white-label program with a prepaid screening commitment, fixed advancement fees, explicit data-outcome permissions, and partner-level service metrics; this would stabilize throughput and cash conversion while making the outcome corpus and workflow integration harder to copy.
main_structural_strength: A prepaid, protocol-specific go/no-go screen sits before costly testing and open-ended claim work, giving the business a cash-first, low-variance control point that is compatible with portfolio batching, automation, and the founder's part-time analytical profile.
primary_score_limiter: The business has no evidence that unrelated partners can supply enough record-complete, contract-eligible, economically valuable cases per batch to sustain the proposed price, margin, repeat rate, and founder-wealth path.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Polish providers already bundle monitoring with manufacturer-warranty handling at low monthly prices, while commercial contract exclusions, manufacturer proof burdens, and costly disconfirming tests can eliminate recovery; this weakens both differentiated willingness to pay and the density of monetizable cases.
